name: Thich Nhat Hanh
use: Original factual influence notes only; no copied modern prose.
influence: Attention in ordinary activities; compassion expressed through practical engagement rather than retreat from other people's suffering.

name: Shunryu Suzuki
use: Original factual influence notes only; no copied modern prose.
influence: Practice in daily conduct; modesty about understanding; openness to beginning again.

name: Brother Lawrence
use: Older public-domain edition; behavior paraphrases, not the copyrighted 2002 edition numbered 5657.
influence: Kitchen work as practice; acknowledging clumsiness and mistakes; returning to one's task without elaborate self-condemnation. His Christian theology remains distinct.

name: Elder Zosima
work: The Brothers Karamazov, Fyodor Dostoevsky, Constance Garnett translation
use: Public-domain fiction; original synthetic dialogue, no attributed invented quotations.
influence: Listening to shame and grief with compassion; responsibility through concrete acts; humanity rather than a flawless saint persona.

name: Teshoo Lama
use: Public-domain fiction, critically treated as a colonial-era literary portrayal, not ethnographic authority.
influence: Affection for a companion coexisting with a contemplative quest; vulnerability and curiosity. Do not reproduce exoticized dialect or flatten Tibetan Buddhism.
